title: The American Cancer Society now recommends regular PSA screening for prostate cancer, every two years from age 50
tldr: The American Cancer Society's new guideline recommends a PSA blood test every two years for average-risk men aged 50 to 69, and yearly from 45 for Black men and men with strong family history.
byline: American Cancer Society, The New York Times

title: FDA approves pimicotinib, a once-daily pill, for joint tumors that are hard to remove surgically
tldr: The FDA approved EMD Serono's pimicotinib for symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor after a placebo-controlled trial in which 56% of treated patients responded, against 3.2% on placebo.
byline: FDA, HMP Global Oncology

title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
tldr: In a phase 3 trial of 1,137 people with resected high-risk melanoma, adding a personalized mRNA therapy to pembrolizumab raised two-year recurrence-free survival from 70.0% to 82.2%.
byline: Georgina V. Long Muhammad A. Khattak Helen J. Gogas Dirk Schadendorf Ana Arance Matteo S. Carlino Piotr Rutkowski Gareth Rivalland Antoni Ribas Janice M. Mehnert Patrick A. Ascierto and Michele Del Vecchiothe INTerpath-001 Investigators* · Melanoma Institute Australia
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia
tldr: A cell-by-cell atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from human, macaque and marmoset basal ganglia finds 61 cell types conserved over 76 million years and maps psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk onto specific cells.
byline: Nelson J. Johansen, Yuanyuan Fu, Matthew Schmitz et al. · Allen Institute

title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
tldr: In mice, the gut antibody IgA slows the renewal of the colon lining through a surface protein called DMBT1, and its absence raises susceptibility to colorectal tumors.
byline: Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad et al. · The Rockefeller University

title: Beam's base-edited sickle cell therapy keeps patients free of severe pain crises for a year in its pivotal trial
tldr: Beam Therapeutics says its one-time base-edited cell therapy, risto-cel, met its main goal of 12 months without severe pain crises in a 49-patient single-arm trial, and plans a US filing.
byline: PharmaShots (summary of Beam's press release), BioPharm International

title: A Lancet Psychiatry analysis compares how well 21 antidepressants keep depression at bay over months to years
tldr: Pooling 115 studies longer than 12 weeks, researchers found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine somewhat more likely than fluoxetine to bring lasting improvement; experts call the differences modest.
byline: The New York Times, BBC News

title: Everyone in a 100,000-person All of Us sample carries gene variants that affect medicines, and a quarter got an affected drug
tldr: A Pitt-led analysis of nearly 100,000 genomes found every participant carried at least one drug-relevant variant (median nine), 24.4% had been prescribed an affected drug, and over 17,000 variants were new.
byline: University of Pittsburgh via Medical Xpress, STAT, Science Translational Medicine

title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
tldr: In lab-grown human neurons lacking the ALS protein TDP-43, fixing one splicing error in the synapse gene UNC13A with an antisense drug restored communication between neurons.
byline: Matthew J. Keuss, Peter Harley, Eugeni Ryadnov et al. · King's College London; University College London; Francis Crick Institute; Leibniz-FMP; Trace Neuroscience

title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
tldr: Yearly stored blood samples show that in two-thirds of women who later got acute myeloid leukaemia, the first driver mutation arose before age 20, and mutant clones then grew predictably.
byline: Caroline J. Watson, Gladys Y. P. Poon, Hamish A. J. MacGregor et al. · University of Cambridge; University College London

title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
tldr: GPS-tracked tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil carried more microplastics in their blood when their home ranges held more human disturbance or lay nearer waste facilities.
byline: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, Arnaud L. J. Desbiez, Mario Henrique Alves et al. · University of British Columbia (Kelowna); Center for Advanced Systems Understanding (CASUS), Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf

title: FDA orders a rare optic-nerve warning on all GLP-1 drugs
tldr: The FDA will require every GLP-1 medicine to carry a warning of a potential increased risk of NAION, a rare condition that can cause permanent vision loss in one eye.
byline: FDA, CBS News

title: FDA approves asundexian, the first factor XIa blocker, to prevent a second stroke
tldr: The FDA approved Bayer's once-daily pill Sunharbo (asundexian) alongside antiplatelet therapy after a mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic stroke or high-risk TIA, after a 12,327-person trial showed a 26% lower risk of ischemic stroke.
byline: FDA, pharmaphorum

title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
tldr: In 4,368 people with prior stroke or TIA, aiming for systolic blood pressure under 120 mm Hg rather than 140 cut major cardiovascular events by 21%, at the cost of more kidney-function events.
byline: Gisele Sampaio Silva M. Julia Machline-Carrion Karla Santo João Brainer Clares de Andrade Eduardo Martins Patrícia Oliveira Guimarães Frederico Monfardini Josué Nieri Silvia R.L. title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease
tldr: Monthly ziltivekimab, an IL-6 antibody, sharply cut inflammatory markers in 6,376 people with atherosclerosis and kidney disease but did not change heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death.
byline: Paul M Ridker A. Michael Lincoff Nikolaus Marx Ann Marie Navar Naveed Sattar Katherine R. Tuttle Matthew Budoff Morten Böttcher Matthew A. Cavender Robin P. Choudhury Jan H. title: A single–amino acid difference between rodent and human Andes virus affects viral glycoprotein trafficking
tldr: One amino acid differs between rodent and human Andes virus glycoproteins, and swapping it changed how long the protein stays in the Golgi and how fast virus-like particles are released in human cells.
byline: Santiago Vidal-Freire, Natalia M. Ferressini-Gerpe, Carla M. Bellomo et al. · Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; Administración Nacional de Laboratorios e Institutos de Salud Dr. Carlos G. Malbrán (ANLIS); Centro Ciencia y Vida and Universidad San Sebastián; U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases; National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

title: Lp(a)-lowering drug pelacarsen cuts the target by 78% but not heart attacks or strokes, in a large phase 3 trial
tldr: In Lp(a)HORIZON, pelacarsen lowered lipoprotein(a) by about 78% in over 8,300 people with heart disease, yet heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths occurred at the same rate as on placebo.
byline: American Heart Association, Healio, American College of Cardiology

title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
tldr: In a randomized trial of about 1,880 adults over 70 without heart disease, stopping statins was statistically noninferior over two years, but cardiovascular events were more frequent over longer follow-up.
byline: Nicolas Rodondi Moa Lina Haller Julia Bianca Bardoczi Luise Adam Manuel Raphael Blum Baris Gencer Tamar Itach Julian Simon Flury Lara Aurora Brockhus Philipp Stefan Aebi Martin Feller Claudia Gregoriano Roxane de la Harpe Jacobijn Gussekloo Nathalie Schwab Pierre Poulizac Simon Pieter Mooijaart Jürg-Hans Beer Stéphanie Baggio Sebastian Carballo Fabrice Bonnet Dina Zekry Luca Gabutti Maria Monika Wertli Drahomir Aujesky Douglas Charles Bauer Rita Fran Redberg Philip Greenland Rosalinde Klazina Elisabeth Poortvliet Philipp Schuetz Marie Méan Alan Gary Haynes and Sven Trellethe STREAM Investigators*

title: Noise pollution alters the body or behavior of 80% of animal species studied, a Science analysis finds
tldr: A pooled analysis of 214 experiments on 177 species found human-made noise changed physiology or behavior in eight of ten species and cut animal numbers by about 37% in noisy areas.
byline: Phys.org, Science (study DOI)

title: Parkinson's may be driven by a vicious cycle that clogs the brain's waste drainage
tldr: Misfolded alpha-synuclein appears to inflame the lymphatic vessels that drain the brain, which then clear it less well, in human tissue and mice.
byline: New Scientist, Journal of Experimental Medicine (study)

title: FDA grants accelerated approval to a subcutaneous antibody for previously treated head and neck cancer
tldr: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after chemotherapy and immunotherapy, based on a 42% response rate in 102 patients.
byline: FDA, Johnson & Johnson (OrigAMI-4 results release)

title: A hair and 1,000 seeds from a Siberian tomb give the oldest directly dated evidence of cannabis intoxication
tldr: Archaeologists found about 1,000 cannabis seeds and hair carrying a breakdown product of THC in a Scythian princely tomb in Siberia, dated to the early eighth century B.C., in a study in Science.
byline: University of Bern, New Scientist, Scientific American

title: British health worker with Ebola flown home as the Congo outbreak passes 10,000 cases
tldr: A British healthcare worker infected in DR Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the first British case of an outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and has no approved treatment.
byline: The Guardian, ECDC

title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
tldr: Researchers built the largest map yet of how essential genes interact in the tuberculosis bacterium, finding nearly 6,500 interactions that could guide new drug targets and antibiotic combinations.
byline: Isaac J. Kresse, Natalie Y. Sayegh, Vanisha Munsamy-Govender et al. · Rockefeller University

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
tldr: A global analysis of 45 threats to more than 21,000 freshwater species finds farming, dams and agricultural runoff dominate, and that freshwater species face higher threat on average than land species.
byline: Christophe Brabant, Laura Pollock, Jonas Geldmann et al. · McGill University

title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
tldr: A large international randomized trial found no evidence that prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improves ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome.
byline: Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz et al.

title: First measles death in New York State in 30 years
tldr: A child in Lewis County, New York, died of measles, the state's first measles death in 30 years, as US cases reach their highest level in about 35 years.
byline: The Guardian, CIDRAP, Gothamist

title: FDA finalizes potency guidance for cell and gene therapies
tldr: The FDA issued final guidance telling makers of cell and gene therapies to build a plan proving that every batch is potent before it reaches a patient.
byline: FDA

title: English A&Es to use early warning scores for sick children
tldr: NHS England is introducing a vital-signs scoring system for children in emergency departments this winter, with parents' concerns able to trigger urgent review regardless of score.
byline: The Guardian, BBC News

title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
tldr: In a randomized trial of 744 older adults with moderate aortic stenosis and risk features, early valve replacement cut two-year death or heart failure events from 23.9% to 16.7%.
byline: Philippe Généreux Raj R. Makkar Philippe Pibarot Jeroen J. Bax Brian R. Lindman Kamran Muhammad J. Bradley Oldemeyer Mark Pirwitz Colin M. Barker Vinod H. Thourani Pradeep K.
